semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {وَكَمْ مِّن مَّلَكٍ}: Here كم is khabarī (declarative) and conveys multiplicity, and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ولا تُغْني شفاعتُهم» is the khabar (predicate). The majority read the word for intercession in the singular (الشفاعة) while the pronoun is plural, in view of the meaning of مَلَك (angel) and the meaning of «كم». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «شفاعتُه» in the singular, taking into account the form of «كم» and of «مَلَكَ». Ibn Miqsam read «شفاعاتُهم» in the plural. And «شيئاً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is: something of benefit (ighnāʾ).

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {وَمَا لَهُم بِهِ}: that is, about what they say, or about that. Makkī said: "The hāʾ refers back to the noun, because the naming (tasmiya) and the name (ism) have the same meaning." Ubayy read «بها», that is, about the angels or about the naming, and this strengthens Makkī's statement.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ), that is: turn away from him and do not confront him; «إنَّ ربك هو أعلمُ [بالضالِّ]»." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "It is as if he is saying: it is a parenthetical clause between «فأعرِضْ» and «إنَّ ربك», but what he says about its being parenthetical is not clear." I (al-Samīn) say: How can he say "as if he is saying: it is parenthetical", with the particle of comparison, when he stated it outright and was explicit, saying: "that is, turn away from him and do not confront him; indeed your Lord…"? And as for his saying "it is not clear", I do not know how it can be unclear when it is plain that this is a reason for that, that is: his saying «إنَّ ربَّك» is the reason for his saying «فأعْرِضْ», and a parenthetical clause between the reason and the thing caused is evident. If they say of something that comes in the middle of a story, "this is parenthetical", how much more so what comes between a reason and its effect?
And his saying: {أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ}: Makkī allowed that it be in its normal sense of comparison (tafḍīl), that is: He knows better than anyone, with these two descriptions and others as well; and that it be in the sense of ʿālim (knowing). A parallel to this has been mentioned repeatedly.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {لِيَجْزِيَ}: There are several views about this lām. First: that it is attached to His saying {لاَ تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ}; Makkī mentioned it. It is remote both in wording and in meaning. Second: that it is attached to what is indicated by His saying {وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السماوات}, that is: to Him belongs the dominion of both, He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, in order to requite the doer of good and the doer of evil. Third: that it is attached to His saying «بمنْ ضَلَّ وبمَنْ اهتدى», and the lām is the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra), that is: the final outcome of the affair of all of them is requital for what they did; al-Zamakhsharī stated this meaning. Fourth: that it is attached to what is indicated by His saying {أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ}, that is: He preserved that in order to requite; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «لنجزيَ، ونجزيَ» with the nūn of majesty, while the rest read with the yāʾ of the third person.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {الذين يَجْتَنِبُونَ}: It may be accusative as a badal (substitute), or as a bayān (explicative), or as a naʿt (adjective) of {الذين أحسنوا}, or by the implied verb أَعْني ("I mean"); and it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are those who…". The disagreement about «كبائر» and «كبير الإِثم» has already been discussed.
His saying: {إِلاَّ اللمم}: There are several views on it. One: that it is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because al-lamam means minor sins, so it is not included in what precedes it; a group said this and it is the well-known view. Two: that it is a ṣifa (adjective) and «إلاَّ» stands in the position of «غير», as in His saying {لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ آلِهَةٌ إِلاَّ الله} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 22], that is: the major sins and indecencies other than al-lamam. Three: that it is a continuous exception (muttaṣil), and this is according to those who explain al-lamam as something other than minor sins; the disagreement is recorded in the books of tafsīr. The basic meaning of al-lamam is what is little and small; from it comes al-lamam, which is a touch of madness; and alamma bi-l-makān means he stayed there only a little; alamma bi-l-ṭaʿām means he ate little of it. Abū al-ʿAbbās said: "The basic meaning of al-lamam is that one draws near something without committing it; one says alamma bi-kadhā when one came near it without mixing with it." Al-Azharī said: "The Arabs use ilmām in the sense of nearness and proximity." Jarīr said: 4134 - بنفسي مَنْ تجنُّبُه عزيزٌ ... عليَّ ومَنْ زيارَتُه لِمامُ (May I give my life for the one whose avoidance is hard on me, and whose visit is only brief.)
And another said:
4135 - متى تأتِنا تُلْمِمْ بنا في ديارِنا ... تَجِدْ حَطَباً جَزْلاً وناراً تَأجَّجا
(Whenever you come to us and visit us in our homes, you will find thick firewood and a blazing fire.)
And another said:
4136 - لقاءُ أخِلاَّءِ الصَّفاءِ لِمامُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The meeting of sincere friends is brief … [Translator's note: the rest of the verse is elided in the source].)
From it also comes limmat al-shaʿr, hair that is shorter than the wafra (hair reaching the ears).
His saying: {أَجِنَّةٌ}: the plural of janīn, which is the child carried in the womb, because it is hidden. Janīn and ajinna follow the pattern of sarīr and asirra.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {وأكدى}: Its origin is from akdā al-ḥāfir, said when someone digging strikes a hard piece of ground (kudya) which stops him from digging; similar is ajbala, that is: he met a mountain which stopped him from digging. And kudiyat aṣābiʿuhu means his fingers grew weary from shaking. Then it came to be used for anyone who seeks something and does not reach it or does not complete it. And «أَرَأَيْتَ» means "tell me".

semin-durr:35-35.t:
And {أَعِندَهُ عِلْمُ}: it is the second object; the first object is omitted by way of restriction, for أعطى.
His saying: «فهو يَرَى»: this clause follows from what precedes it in an obvious sequence. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«فهو يرى» is a nominal sentence standing in the place of a verbal one. The original is: «أَعنده عِلْمُ الغيبِ فيَرى»; and had it come in that form, it would have been accusative as the answer to the question." End of quotation. This is unnecessary, given that the sequence is evident with the nominal sentence; he has a parallel to this statement elsewhere, and the reply to it has already been given.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ}: conjoined (ʿaṭf) to «موسى». He singled out these two prophets, peace be upon them, for mention because between Ibrāhīm and Mūsā a man used to be seized for the offence of another; so the first to oppose them was Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. And «أم» is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿa), that is: "rather, has he not been informed". The majority read «وَفَّى» with shadda. Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn al-Samayfiʿ read «وَفَى» without shadda. It has already been mentioned that there are three dialectal forms of it. He left tawfiya and wafāʾ unrestricted so that they would cover everything that he fulfilled.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {أَلاَّ تَزِرُ}: «أَنْ» is the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», and its noun is omitted, being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). «ولا تزرُ» is the khabar, and negation was used because the khabar is a verbal clause with a fully conjugated verb not accompanied by «قد», as was explained in sūrat al-Māʾida. As for «أنْ» and what lies within its scope, there are two views, the more apparent being: genitive, as a badal of «ما» in His saying {بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ}. The second: nominative, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "that is [the content]: that no bearer shall bear…" or "it is: that no bearer shall bear…"; and it is an answer to an implied question, as if someone said: "And what is in their scrolls?" and so it was answered with that. I (al-Samīn) say: It may also be accusative, by the implied verb أعني ("I mean"), as an answer to that questioner. And in every place where this mubtadaʾ is implied in this sense, this verb may be implied.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {وَأَن لَّيْسَ}: This too is the lightened «أنْ». No separation is made here between it and the verb, because the verb is not conjugated. Its position is genitive, nominative or accusative, because it is conjoined to the «أَنْ» before it; likewise the position of «وأَنَّ سَعْيَه». And «يُرَى» is passive, so it may be from the verbs of sight, that is: "is seen", or from the verbs of knowing, in which case the second object is omitted, that is: "is seen as present"; the first is clearer. Makkī said: "Al-Zajjāj allowed «يَرى» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, with an implied hāʾ, that is: 'he will soon see it'. The Kufans did not allow it, because «سَعْيَه» would then have both «أنَّ» and «يَرى» operating on it; but it is permissible according to al-Mubarrad and others, since the entry of «أنَّ» upon «سَعْيَه» and its operation indicates that the omitted hāʾ belongs to «يَرَى»; and on this basis the Basrans allowed «إنَّ زيداً ضربْتُ» without a hāʾ."
I (al-Samīn) say: This is a weak disagreement. They imagined that two operators of different kinds were directed at the noun; I say "different kinds" because the view of some of them is that two verbs may operate on a single governed word, and from this comes the chapter of tanāzuʿ (rival governance) in some of its forms, such as «قام وقعد زيدٌ» and «ضربْتُ وأكرمْتُ عَمْراً»; and that a single operator may operate on a noun and on its pronoun together, such as «زيداً ضربتُه» in the chapter of ishtighāl. This is a false imagining, because we say: «سَعْيَه» is accusative by «أنَّ», and «يَرى» has power over its implied pronoun.
I say: The apparent sense of this is that it was not read this way; yet Abū al-Baqāʾ reported that it was read so as a shādhdh (irregular) reading, but he weakened it on another ground. He said: "It was read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and it is weak, because it contains no pronoun referring to the noun of «أنَّ», which is al-saʿy, and the pronoun in it is for the hāʾ, so the noun is left without a khabar. It is like your saying «إنَّ غلامَ زيدٍ قامَ» when you mean 'Zayd stood': then ghulām has no khabar. It has been explained on the basis that the implied form is 'he will soon see it', so that the hāʾ refers back to al-saʿy, but this is remote." End of quotation. I wish I knew how he imagined the aforementioned obstacle, and how he made it analogous to what he mentioned! Then what remoteness is there in the implied form "he will soon see his own striving"? It is as though he had come across the Kufans' doctrine of prohibition, except that the one who perceives is not the same as the one who is perceived.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ}: Two views are allowed. The more apparent: that the nominative pronoun refers to al-insān (man) and the accusative one to his striving; and al-jazāʾ is a maṣdar showing the kind. The second: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is allowed that the pronoun be for al-jazāʾ, and then He explained it by His saying «الجزاءَ», or made it a badal of it, like His saying {وَأَسَرُّواْ النجوى الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 3]." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "If it is an explanation of the accusative pronoun in «يُجْزاه», then on what is it accusative? And if it is a badal, it is a badal of the overt noun from a pronoun, which is a disputed question, and the sound view is prohibition."
I (al-Samīn) say: It is astonishing how he can say, "on what is it accusative?" Its being accusative is from two aspects. One, which is the apparent and clear one: that it be an ʿaṭf bayān, and ʿaṭf bayān can truthfully be called an explanation (mufassir), which is a permissible and common expression. The second: that it be accusative by the implied verb أَعْني, which is also a permissible expression; they call such a thing an explanation. Abū al-Baqāʾ prohibited «الجزاء الأوفى» from being accusative as a maṣdar. He said: "«الجزاءَ الأوفى» is the object of «يُجْزاه» and not a maṣdar, because He described it as «الأَوْفى», and that is a description of what is requited, not a description of the act." I say: This is not far from error, because it would require that يُجْزى take three objects. The explanation: the first stands in the place of the agent, the second is the hāʾ which is the pronoun of al-saʿy, and the third is «الجزاءَ الأوفى». Also, how would the meaning be coherent? It may be answered that he meant it to be a badal of the hāʾ, as was reported earlier from al-Zamakhsharī, so that it can be said to be the object of «يُجْزاه» and then it would not take three objects; but this is far from his purpose, and such a thing is an enigma. As for his statement "al-awfā is not among the attributes of the act", it is disputed; rather it is among its attributes figuratively, just as what is requited is described by it figuratively, for the literal sense is negated in both, and only the one who is requited is literally described by it.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {وَأَنَّ إلى رَبِّكَ}: The majority read this hamza with fatḥa, and what is conjoined to it, meaning that all of it is in the scrolls of Mūsā and Ibrāhīm. Abū al-Sammāl read all of them with kasra, as a new beginning (ibtidāʾ). And His saying «أَضْحك وأَبْكى» and what follows: the rhetoricians call this ṭibāq (antithesis) and taḍādd (opposition), which is a type of badīʿ (embellishment): two opposites, contradictories or incompatibles in some respect are mentioned together.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {أقنى}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "He gave al-qunya, which is wealth that you have accumulated and resolved not to let leave your hand." Al-Jawharī said: "qaniya al-rajul yaqnā qinan, like ghaniya yaghnā ghinan." Then it becomes transitive by a change of vowel, so one says qanaytu mālan, that is: I earned it; this is parallel to shatirat ʿaynuhu (with kasra) and shatarahā Allāh (with fatḥa). When the hamza or doubling enters it, it takes a second object, so one says aqnāhu Allāh mālan and qannāhu iyyāhu, that is: He made him earn it. The poet said:
4137 - كم مِنْ غنيٍّ أصاب الدهرُ ثَرْوَته ... ومِنْ فقيرٍ تَقَنَّى بعد إقْلالِ
(How many a rich man whose wealth fortune has struck, and how many a poor man who acquired wealth after poverty.)
That is: he acquired wealth, so the second object was omitted. The two objects of aghnā and aqnā are omitted, because the intention is to attribute these two acts to Him alone; the same applies to the remaining ones.
The alif of «أَقْنى» is from yāʾ, because it comes from al-qunya. He said:
4138 - ألا إنَّ بَعْد العُدْمِ للمَرْءِ قُنِيَةً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Indeed, after poverty a man has acquired wealth …)
It was also said: aqnā means "He made content". Al-Rāghib said: "The verification of it is that He gave him an acquisition (qunya) of contentment. And qanaytu kadhā and iqtanaytuhu." He said:
4139 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
قَنِيْتُ حَيائي عِفَّةً وتَكَرُّما
(I kept my modesty as chastity and nobility.) [Translator's note: the entry ends here in the source, apparently incomplete.]

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {رَبُّ الشعرى}: In the language of the Arabs, al-Shiʿrā refers to two stars, one of which is called al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr, and this is what is meant in the noble verse, since Khuzāʿa used to worship it; its worship was instituted by Abū Kabsha, a man among their leaders. Quraysh used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "Abū Kabsha", likening him to that man in that he had introduced a religion other than their religion. Al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr rises after Orion (al-Jawzāʾ) in the intensity of heat, and it is called Mirzam al-Jawzāʾ and also "the dog of the Giant" (kalb al-jabbār). The second is al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumayṣāʾ, which is the one in the Arm (al-dhirāʿ). The reason for their naming them so is what the Arabs claimed: that the two were sisters, or two wives, of Suhayl; Suhayl descended towards Yemen, and al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr followed him and crossed the Milky Way (al-majarra), so she was called al-ʿAbūr ("the crosser"); al-Ghumayṣāʾ stayed and wept at his loss until her eye became bleary (ghamiṣat), and for that reason she is dimmer than al-ʿAbūr.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {عَاداً الأولى}: Know that this noble verse is among the most problematic verses in transmission and in explanation. Allah the Exalted has made it easy to work all of that out by His might and power, so I say: The readers differed on this in four ranks.
First: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and the Kufans read «عادَاً الأُولى» with tanwīn carrying kasra, a sukūn on the lām, and a fully pronounced hamza after it; all this is in continuous reading (waṣl). When they stop at «عاداً» and begin with «الأُوْلى», then by their analogy they say «الأولى» with a hamzat al-waṣl, a sukūn on the lām and a fully pronounced hamza.
Second: Qālūn read «عاداً لُّؤْلَى», assimilating the tanwīn into the lām, transferring the vowel of the hamza to the lām of definiteness, and pronouncing the wāw as a hamza; this is in continuous reading. As for beginning with «الأولى», he has three ways. The first: «الُّؤْلَى» with a hamzat al-waṣl, then a lām with ḍamma, then a hamza with sukūn. The second: «لُؤْلَى» with a lām carrying ḍamma, then a hamza with sukūn. The third: like the beginning of Ibn Kathīr and those with him.
Third: Warsh read «عاداً لُّوْلى», assimilating the tanwīn into the lām and transferring the vowel of the hamza to it as Qālūn does, except that he left the wāw as it is, not changed into a hamza; this is in continuous reading. As for beginning with it, he has two ways: «ألُّوْلَى» with the hamza and the transfer, and «لُوْلَى» with the transfer without a hamzat al-waṣl; the wāw stays as it is with sukūn in these two ways.
Fourth: Abū ʿAmr read like Warsh both in continuous reading and in beginning, exactly alike, except that he adds to it in the beginning a third way, which is the way of Ibn Kathīr and those mentioned with him. So the result is that Qālūn and Abū ʿAmr each have three ways in beginning, and Warsh has two. Consider this, for working it out from the books of qirāʾāt is difficult to grasp. This is what relates to the readings.
As for explaining them, it depends on knowing three principles. First: the rule of tanwīn when a sākin (letter with sukūn) follows it. Second: the rule of the transferred vowel. Third: what is the origin of «أُوْلَى»? As for the first, the rule for tanwīn that meets one is that it takes kasra because of the meeting of two sākins, as in {قُلْ هُوَ الله أَحَدٌ} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 1], or is dropped by analogy with a weak letter, as in the reading {أَحَدٌ الله الصمد}, and as in the poet's saying:
4140 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلاَّ قليلاً
(… nor one who remembers Allah except a little.)
This is very rare, and its verification has already passed. As for the second, the Arabs have two practices regarding the transferred vowel: counting the vowel (iʿtidād) and not counting it, the latter being the higher dialect. As for the third, «أُوْلَى» is the feminine of «أَوَّل», and the disagreement about its origin was given in full at the beginning of this work, so refer to it. Once these three principles are established, I say:
As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr and those with him, they made «عاداً» fully declinable: either because it is the name of a tribe or of the father, so nothing in it prevents it, or because it was feminine, the name of a tribe or of the mother, but like Hind and Daʿd, in which both declining it and not declining it are allowed; so it is like the poet's saying:
4141 - لم تَتَلَفَّعْ بفَضْلِ مِئْزَرِها ... دَعْدٌ ولم تُسْقَ دعدُ في العُلَب
(Daʿd did not wrap herself in the excess of her wrapper, and Daʿd was not given drink from the milk-bowls.)
He declined it first and did not decline it second. They did not transfer the vowel of the hamza to the lām of definiteness, so two sākins met; so they gave the tanwīn kasra because of their meeting, according to the well-known practice of the two dialects, and dropped the hamzat al-waṣl of «الأُوْلى» since the vowel of the tanwīn made it unnecessary in continuous reading. When they begin with it, they need the hamzat al-waṣl, so they bring it and say «الأُوْلى», like its counterparts among hamzat al-waṣl. This is a clear reading with no difficulty, and for that reason the great multitude chose it.
As for the reading of those who assimilated the tanwīn into the lām of definiteness, who are Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr (with differences between them in some things, as explained earlier), its explanation is counting the transferred vowel. That is because among the Arabs there are those who, when they transfer the vowel of the hamza to a sākin before it, such as the lām of definiteness, treat it as still having sukūn and do not count the transferred vowel; so they give kasra to the sākin before it, do not assimilate the tanwīn into it, and bring a hamzat al-waṣl before it. So he says: «لم يَذْهَبِ لَحْمَرُ» and «رأيت زياداً لَعْجَم», without assimilating the tanwīn, with al-aḥmar and al-aʿjam having the hamzat al-waṣl, since the lām has the status of a sākin; this is the well-known dialect. And among them are those who count it: they do not give kasra to the first sākin, do not bring the hamzat al-waṣl, and assimilate the tanwīn into the lām of definiteness, so he says «لم يَذْهَبْ لَحْمر» with sukūn on the bāʾ, and «لَحْمَرُ» and «لَعْجَمُ» without hamza, and «زيادُ لّعجم» with shadda on the lām; and this reading came according to this dialect. This is in summary.
In detail, I say: As for Qālūn, he transferred the vowel of the hamza to the lām of definiteness, even though transfer is not his general practice, because he intended lightness by assimilation; and when he transferred the vowel he counted it, since assimilation is not possible into a sākin or into what has its status.
As for his pronouncing the wāw as a hamza, two transmitted explanations are given. One: that «أُوْلى» has for him the origin «وُؤْلَى», from waʾala, meaning "he escaped", as is the view of the Kufans; then he changed the wāw to a hamza because it is a wāw with ḍamma, and it was mentioned to you earlier that this is a regular dialect; so two hamzas met, the second with sukūn, and it had to be turned into a wāw, as in «أُوْمِنُ». When the first hamza was dropped because its vowel was transferred, the second returned to its origin as a hamza, because it had been turned into a wāw only on account of the first, which had now gone. This, as you see, is forced and has no evidence. The second: that when he transferred the vowel to the lām, the ḍamma came before the wāw as though it were on it, since the vowel of a letter is right before it, so he changed the wāw to a hamza, as in the poet's saying:
4142 - أَحَبُّ المُؤْقِدِيْنَ إليَّ موسى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The dearest of the fire-kindlers to me is Mūsā …)
and as in the reading «يُؤْقنون» and the pronouncing of «السُّؤْقِ» and «سُؤْقِه» as hamza, the verification of which has already been given; and this is based on his counting the vowel as well. In this explanation there is no evidence for what the origin of «أُوْلى» is for him, so the whole disagreement mentioned remains possible. As for his beginning the word without transfer, that is the original; and because he transferred in continuous reading only to achieve lightness by assimilation, and there is no assimilation in beginning, there is no need for the transfer. And as for his beginning with the transfer, it is because it is carried over from continuous reading, so that the pronunciation runs the same course in both.
The reason for keeping the alif of waṣl along with the transfer in one of the two ways is not counting the vowel of the lām, according to what the reading has in its counterparts where transfer is found; for the aim is only that the pronunciation in beginning and in continuous reading run the same course, and that is achieved by mere transfer even if the two differ as to counting the vowel or not. The reason for not bringing the alif in the second way is carrying beginning over to continuous reading in both transfer and counting the vowel. This way is strengthened by the writing of «الأولى» in this place without an alif. And the discussion of pronouncing the wāw as a hamza with transfer in beginning is like the discussion of it in continuous reading, as above.
As for Warsh, his principle is to transfer the vowel of the hamza to the lām in continuous reading, so he transferred according to his principle, except that he counted the vowel so that his intention of lightness by assimilation would hold, and counting the vowel in such cases is not his principle. Do you not see that he drops the alif in {سِيَرتَهَا الأولى} [Ṭāhā: 21] and {وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الأشقى} [al-Aʿlā: 11]? Had he counted the vowel he would not have dropped it. As for what came from him in some transmissions, {قَالُواْ لآنَ جِئْتَ بالحق} [al-Baqara: 71], it is a rare way, explained by following the report and combining the two dialects. His beginning with the transfer is also according to his principle in that, and his beginning with the alif of waṣl is by not counting the vowel, since there is no need to intend that in beginning; and not bringing the alif for him is by counting the vowel, carrying beginning over to continuous reading and also agreeing with the writing; he does not begin with the original, since that is not his principle; and «الأُوْلَى» in his reading admits the disagreement mentioned about its origin.
As for Abū ʿAmr, the reason for his reading in continuous reading and beginning is as given earlier for Qālūn, except that he differs from him in pronouncing the wāw as a hamza, because he did not give it the rule of what is next to it; and for him it is not from waʾala but from another source, as the disagreement about it was given to you at the beginning of this subject. It is also possible that its origin for him is from waʾala too, but he substituted in the case of transfer to go further in lightness, or to agree with the case of not transferring. Abū ʿUthmān and Abū al-ʿAbbās faulted this reading, I mean the reading of assimilation, holding that the eloquent dialect is not to count what is incidental; but no regard is to be paid to their rejection since it is established as a dialect and a reading, even if another is more eloquent than it. It is established from the Arabs that they say «الَحْمَر» and «لَحْمَر» with and without the hamzat al-waṣl along with the transfer. And Allah knows best.
Ubayy read, and it is so in his codex, «عادَ الأُولى», not fully declined, taking it to be the tribe or the mother as above, so it has both being a proper name (ʿalamiyya) and feminine gender; and the feminine is indicated by His saying «الأُوْلَى», for He described it with the description of the feminine.

semin-durr:51-51.t: The disagreement about «ثمود» regarding whether it is fully declined or not was given in sūrat Hūd. There are two views on its being accusative here. One: that it is conjoined to «عاداً». The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "and He destroyed"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this and began with it, but there is no need for it. It is not allowed to make it accusative by «أَبْقَى», because what follows the negative «ما» does not operate on what precedes it. The apparent sense is that what «أَبْقَى» is attached to refers to those mentioned before, ʿĀd and Thamūd, that is: "so He did not spare them", that is, ʿĀd and Thamūd; or the implied form is: "so He did not leave any of them, nor an eye that blinks".

semin-durr:52-52.t:
And {قَوْمَ نُوحٍ}: like the one before it. And «مِنْ قبلُ», that is: before ʿĀd and Thamūd.
And His saying {إِنَّهُمْ}: the pronoun may be for the people of Nūḥ specifically, or for all of the three nations mentioned before.
And His saying {كَانُواْ هُمْ}: «هم» may be tawkīd (emphasis) or a faṣl (separating pronoun); that it be a badal is weak. The thing compared to is omitted, its implied form being: "than ʿĀd and Thamūd" on our view that the pronoun is for the people of Nūḥ specifically, and on the view that the pronoun is for all, the implied form is: "than others". And «المُؤْتَفِكَة» is accusative by «أَهْوَى», and it was put first for the sake of the verse endings (fawāṣil).

semin-durr:54-54.t: His saying: {مَا غشى}: like His saying {مَآ أوحى} [al-Najm: 10] in its vagueness, and it is the second object if we say that the doubling is for transitivity; but if we say that it is for intensity and multiplicity, then «ما» is the agent, as in His saying {فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِّنَ اليم مَا غَشِيَهُمْ} [Ṭāhā: 78].

semin-durr:55-55.t: His saying: {فَبِأَيِّ}: attached to «تَتَمارَى», and the bāʾ is locative, meaning "in". Ibn Muḥayṣin and Yaʿqūb read «تَمارى» with omission (of one tāʾ), like the reading «تَذَكَّرون».

semin-durr:56-56.t: And {هذا}: an indication of the verses mentioned before, or of the Qurʾān, or of the Messenger ﷺ. And nadhīr (warner): it may be a maṣdar or an active participle; neither is regular, for the regular form of its maṣdar is indhār and of its active participle mundhir. And al-nudhur may be a plural of nadhīr in its two senses mentioned. And «الأُوْلَى» is an adjective, taken in the sense of a plural, as in His saying {مَآرِبُ} [Ṭāhā: 18]. And al-āzifa, that is: the impending Hour (al-sāʿa al-āzifa), as in His saying {اقتربت الساعة} [al-Qamar: 1]; it may also be that al-āzifa is a proper name for the Resurrection by predominant usage.

semin-durr:58-58.t: His saying: {كَاشِفَةٌ}: it may be an adjective or a maṣdar. If it is an adjective, it is possible that the feminine is because it describes an omitted feminine noun; it was said that the implied form is "a self that uncovers (nafs kāshifa)" or "a state that uncovers (ḥāl kāshifa)"; and it is possible that the tāʾ is for intensification, like ʿallāma and nassāba, that is: there is no human being who is kāshifa, that is, who uncovers much. If it is a maṣdar, it is like al-ʿāfiya, al-ʿāqiba and khāʾinat al-aʿyun. The meaning of kashf here is either from kashafa al-shayʾ, that is: he knew its reality, as in His saying {لاَ يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقْتِهَآ إِلاَّ هُوَ}; or from kashafa al-ḍurr, that is: he removed it, that is: no one but Allah the Exalted can remove it and save from it. The discussion of the root «أزف» was given in sūrat Ghāfir.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {أَفَمِنْ هذا الحديث}: attached to «تَعْجَبون», and iʿmāl (rival governance) does not apply here, because a condition of iʿmāl is that the governed word come after the operators, whereas here it comes before. There is a remote disagreement on it, and the noble verse is derived from it; for each of «تَعْجبون», «وتَضْحكون» and «ولا تَبكون» requires this prepositional phrase in meaning.
The majority read tāʾ, jīm and ḥāʾ with fatḥa in «تَعْجَبون» and «تَضْحكون». Al-Ḥasan read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the jīm and ḥāʾ, without a conjoining wāw between the two verbs, and this is more emphatic, since when they make others laugh their own daring is greater. Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read like the majority, except that they have no conjoining wāw, like al-Ḥasan; so «تضحكون» may be a ḥāl or a resumptive clause, like the one before it.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {وَأَنتُمْ سَامِدُونَ}: this clause may be resumptive, Allah the Exalted informing about them of that; and it may be a ḥāl, that is: pretending to weep is negated for you while you are «سامدونَ». Sumūd was said to mean turning away; it was also said: heedless amusement; it was also said: stiffness; it was also said: arrogance. The poet said:
4143 - رَمَى الحِدْثانُ نِسْوَةَ آلِ سَعْدٍ ... بمقدارٍ سَمَدْن له سُمودا فرَدَّ شعرورَهن السودَ بِيْضاً ... ورَدَّ وجوهَهن البيضَ سُودا
(Fortune struck the women of the family of Saʿd with a decree, and they stood stunned before it; it turned their black hair white and turned their white faces black.)
This is in the sense of stiffness and humility. Another said:
4144 - ألا أيها الإِنسانُ إنَّك سامِدٌ ... كأنَّك لا تَفْنَى ولا أنت هالكُ
(O man, you are heedless, as though you would never perish and were not doomed.)
This is in the sense of one who is amusing himself and playing. Abū ʿUbayda said: "Sumūd is singing in the language of Ḥimyar; they say: 'O girl, usmudī lanā', that is: sing for us." Al-Rāghib said: "Al-sāmid is the one who amuses himself, raising his head, from their saying 'a camel sāmid in its walking'; it was also said: sammada raʾsahu and sabbadahu, that is: he shaved off his hair entirely."

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِذَا هوى}: There are several views on what governs this adverbial, and each has a difficulty. One of the views: that it is accusative by the omitted oath verb, its implied form being "I swear by the star at the time of its falling"; Abū al-Baqāʾ and others said this. It is problematic, because the oath verb is an inshāʾ (performative), and a performative is in the present, while «إذا» is for the future of time, so how can they meet? The second: that its governor is implied, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «النجم», that is, "I swear by it while it is settled in the time of its falling". This is problematic on two counts: first, that «النجم» is a body, and time cannot be a ḥāl for it, just as it cannot be a khabar for it; second, that «إذا» is for the future, so how can it be a ḥāl? The reply to the first: that by «النجم» is meant a portion of the Qur'an, and the Qur'an was revealed in parts over twenty years; this is the exegesis of Ibn ʿAbbās and others. The reply to the second: that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). The third: that its governor is «النجم» itself, when the Qur'an is meant by it; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. There is room for objection in it, because «القرآن» does not govern an adverbial when it is meant as a name for this particular book. It may be said: «النجم» has the sense of «المُنَجَّم» (the revealed in parts), as if it were said: "by the Qur'an revealed in parts at this time". This discussion arises in several places, among them {والشمس وَضُحَاهَا} [الشمس: 1] and what follows it, and His saying {والليل إِذَا يغشى} [الليل: 1], {والضحى والليل إِذَا سجى} [الضحى: 1]. A more specific discussion than this will come in al-Shams, which you will find, if Allah the Exalted wills. It was also said that by «النجم» here is meant the genus, and this was quoted:
4121 - فباتَتْ تَعُدُّ النجمَ في مُسْتَحيرةٍ ... سريعٍ بأيدي الآكلين جمودُها
(She spent the night counting the star in a pool of fat that quickly congeals in the hands of the eaters.)
that is, "counting the stars". It was also said: rather, a specific star is meant. It was said: the Pleiades. It was said: Sirius (al-Shiʿrā), for its mention in His saying {وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ الشعرى} [النجم: 49]. It was said: Venus, because it was worshipped. The correct view is that it is the Pleiades, because this has become a proper name by predominance. From this is the saying of the Arabs: «إذا طَلَعَ النجمُ عِشاءً ابتغى الراعي كِساءً» ("when the star rises in the evening, the shepherd seeks a cloak"). They also said: «طَلَعَ النجمُ غُدْيَة فابتغى الراعي كُسْيَة». «هَوَى يَهْوي هُوِيّاً» means to fall from a height, and «هَوِي يَهْوَى هَوَىً» means to incline in love. Al-Rāghib said: "«الهُوِيُّ» is falling from a height." Then he said: "«الهُوِيُّ» is going down a slope, and «الهوى» is going up", and he quoted:
4122 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يَهْوي مخارِمَها هُوِيَّ الأجدَلِ
(... it swoops down upon its passes with the swoop of the falcon.)
It was also said: «هَوَى» in the language is to pierce the air, its destination being downward, or its ending up there even if it does not aim at it. He said:
4123 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... هُوِيَّ الدَّلْوِ أسْلَمَها الرِّشاءُ
(... the drop of a bucket, the rope having let it go.)
The discussion of this was given in full earlier.

semin-durr:2-2.t: And His saying: {مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ}: this is the answer to the oath. «عن الهوى», that is, "his speech does not proceed from desire", so «عن» is in its usual sense. It was also said: it has the sense of «الباء». There are two views on the fāʿil (agent) of «يَنْطِق»: the first, that it is the pronoun of the Prophet, peace be upon him, which is the apparent one; the second, that it is the pronoun of the Qur'an, as in His saying {هذا كِتَابُنَا يَنطِقُ عَلَيْكُم بالحق} [الجاثية: 29].

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {إِنْ هُوَ}: that is, "what he speaks with is not...", or "the Qur'an is not...".
His saying: {يوحى}: a naʿt (adjective) of «وَحْيٌ». The benefit of bringing this attribute is that it negates figurative sense, that is, it is a revelation in reality, not merely in name, as you say «هذا قولٌ يقال» ("this is a saying that is said"). It was also said that its implied form is «يُوحى إليه», and in it there is added benefit.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ}: It is permissible that this «هاء» be for the Messenger, which is the apparent one, in which case the second object is omitted, that is, "he taught the Messenger the revelation", meaning what is revealed; and permissible that it be for the Qur'an and the revelation, in which case the first object is omitted, that is, "he taught it to the Messenger". As for «شديدُ القُوى», it was said: Jibrīl, which is the apparent one. It was said: the Creator the Exalted, for His saying {الرحمن عَلَّمَ القرآن} [الرحمن: 1-2]. «شديدُ القُوى» is an annexation of the sifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) to its nominative, so it is not a true annexation.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {مِرَّةٍ}: «المِرَّةُ» is strength and might. From it is «أَمْرَرْتُ الحَبْلَ» when you twisted its strands firmly, and «المَرِير» is the rope, as is «المَمَرُّ», as if its twisting were repeated time after time. Quṭrub said: "The Arabs say of everyone of sound judgement and firm intellect: «ذو مِرَّة»", and he quoted:
4124 - وإني لَذو مِرَّةٍ مُرَّةٍ ... إذا رَكِبَتْ خالةٌ خالَها
(I am a man of bitter strength when a maternal aunt rides upon her maternal uncle.)

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وَهُوَ بالأفق}: There are two views on it. The more apparent: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «بالأفق» is its khabar (predicate), the pronoun being for Jibrīl or for the Prophet ﷺ. Then, for this clause there are two views: the first, that this clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «استوى»; Makkī said this. The second, that it is resumptive, the Exalted reporting that. The second view: that «هو» is conjoined to the latent pronoun in «استوى». The pronoun of «استوى» and «هو» are either both for Allah the Exalted, which is the saying of al-Ḥasan; or it was said: the pronoun of «استوى» is for Jibrīl and «هو» for Muḥammad, peace be upon him; or it was said: the reverse. This second view proceeds only on the opinion of the Kufans, because it involves conjunction on an attached nominative pronoun without emphasis or separator. This view is reported from al-Farrāʾ and al-Ṭabarī.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {فتدلى}: «التدلِّي» is extending from above to below, and it is used for nearness from above; al-Farrāʾ and Ibn al-Aʿrābī said this. The Hudhalī said:
4125 - تَدَلَّى علينا وهو زَرْقُ حَمامةٍ ... له طِحْلِبٌ في مُنْتهى القَيْظِ هامِدُ
(He came down upon us, and he is a dove's blue-grey, with algae at the end of the summer heat, still.)
And another said:
4126 - تَدَلَّى عليها بين سِبٍّ وخَيْطَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(He let himself down upon her between a rope and a cord ...)
It is said: «هو كالقِرِلَّى، إن رأى خيراً تدلَّى، وإن لم يَرَه تولَّى» ("he is like the qirilla bird: if it sees good, it comes down, and if it does not, it turns away"). As for «استوى», Makkī said: "It applies to one, and most often applies to two, and for that reason al-Farrāʾ made the pronoun for two."

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {فَكَانَ قَابَ}: here there are omitted muḍāfs that one is compelled to imply, that is, "the measure of the distance of his nearness to him was like the measure of the distance of a «قاب»". Abū ʿAlī did the same with the saying of the poet:
4127 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وقد جَعَلَتْني مِنْ حَزِيْمَةَ إصبعا
(... and she has placed me at a finger's distance from Ḥazīma.)
that is, "of the measure of the distance of a finger". «القابُ» is the measure. You say «هذا قابُ هذا», that is, its measure. Like it are «القِيبُ», «القادُ» and «القِيس». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Measurement has come by the bow, the spear, the whip, the forearm, the fathom, the step, the span, the shibr and the finger; from this: 'there is no prayer until the sun rises the measure of two spears.' And in the hadith: «لَقابُ قوس أحدِكم من الجنة وموضعُ قِدِّه خيرٌ من الدنيا وما فيها» ('the space of one of your bows in Paradise, and the place of his whip, is better than the world and what is in it'); «القِدُّ» is the whip. The «ألف» of «قاب» is from a «واو»; Abū al-Baqāʾ stated this. As for «قِيْبٌ», it gives no indication that it is a «ياء», because a «واو» preceded by kasra is changed into «ياء», like «دِيْمة» and «قِيمة». Al-Rāghib also mentioned it under the root «قوب», but he said in explaining it: 'It is what is between the grip and the curve of the bow', so on this it would be the measure of half a bow, because the grip is at its middle. «السِّيَةُ» is the notch in which the string is set." There is an objection in what he said that is not hidden. It is reported from Mujāhid that it is from the string to the grip of the bow at its middle. It was also said: the bow is a forearm's length by which one measures; this was reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, and that it is a dialect of the Hijazis.
«القَوْسُ» is well known and is feminine; they deviated in forming its diminutive, saying «قُوَيْس» without feminine mark, like «عُرَيْب» and «حُرَيْب»; its plural is «قِسِيّ», which is a transposition of «قُوُوْس», and its morphology has a place elsewhere.
His saying: {أَوْ أدنى}: it is like His saying {أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ} [الصافات: 147], because the meaning is: it was at one of these two measures in the view of the beholder; that is, because of the closeness of what is between them, the beholder is in doubt about that. «أدنى» is a comparative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), and what it is compared with is omitted, that is, "or nearer than the length of two bows".

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {فأوحى}: that is, Allah, even though no mention of Him has preceded, since there is no confusion. His saying «ما أَوْحى» is left vague to magnify it and raise its status. Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik used it as evidence that it is not a condition for the ṣila (relative clause) that it be known to the addressee. Like it is {فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِّنَ اليم مَا غَشِيَهُمْ} [طه: 78]; but this condition is the well-known one among the grammarians.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {مَا كَذَبَ}: Hishām read it with shadda on the «دال»; the rest read it light. As for the first [reading], its meaning is that what Muḥammad ﷺ saw with his eye, his heart confirmed and did not deny, that is, it did not say to him: "I did not recognise you." «ما» is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the returning pronoun is omitted. So the fāʿil (agent) of «رأى» is a pronoun returning to the Prophet ﷺ. As for the light reading, the same was said of it. «كذَبَ» is transitive by itself. It was also said: it is on the basis of dropping the preposition, that is, "in what he saw"; Makkī and others said this. Two views were allowed for «ما»: the first, that it has the sense of «الذي»; the second, that it is a maṣdar particle. It is also permissible that the fāʿil of «رأى» be a pronoun returning to the heart, that is, "his heart did not doubt what he saw with his eye".

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ}: The two (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «أَفَتَمْرُوْنَه» with fatḥa on the «تاء» and sukūn on the «ميم»; the rest read «تُمارونه». ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and al-Shaʿbī read «أَفَتُمْرُوْنَه» with ḍamma on the «تاء» and sukūn on the «ميم». As for the first, there are two views on it. The first: that it is from «مَرَيْتُه حَقَّهُ» when you overcame him and denied him it. It was made transitive by «على» because it includes the sense of overcoming. And this was quoted:
4128 - لَئِن هَجَرْتَ أخا صدقٍ ومَكْرُمَةٍ ... لقد مَرَيْتَ أخاً ما كان يَمْرِيكا
(If you have forsaken a brother of truth and nobility, you have wronged a brother who never wronged you.)
because when he denies him his right, he has overcome him over it. The second: that it is from «مَراه على كذا», that is, he overcame him over it, so it is from «المِراء», which is disputation. As for the second reading, it is from «ماراه يُماريه مُراءاة», that is, he disputed with him. Its derivation is from milking the she-camel («مَرْي الناقة»), because each of the two disputants draws out what the other has. Its proper construction would be with «في», as you say «جادَلْتُه في كذا», but it was made to include the sense of overcoming and was made transitive in the same way. As for the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, it is from «أمراه», quadriliteral.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {نَزْلَةً أخرى}: There are three views on it. The first: that it is accusative as an adverbial. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The accusative of the adverbial that is «مرة»; because «الفَعْلَة» is the name of the single occurrence from the verb, so it is in its ruling." I say: this is not the school of the Basrans, but only the school of al-Farrāʾ; Makkī reported it from him. The second: that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). Makkī said: "that is, he saw him descending another descent"; al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya took this view. The third: that it is accusative as a maṣdar of emphasis, which Abū al-Baqāʾ implied as "another time or another seeing". I say: there is room for objection in interpreting «نَزْلَةً» as a seeing. «أخرى» indicates a seeing that preceded it.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {عِندَ سِدْرَةِ}: an adverbial for «رَآه». «عندها جنةُ» is an inceptive clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is better that the ḥāl be the adverbial, and «جَنَّةُ المَأْوى» be the fāʿil (agent) by it. The majority read «جنَّة» as a noun, nominative. The Commander of the Believers, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Abū Hurayra, Ibn al-Zubayr, Anas, Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb read «جَنَّة» as a past verb. The «هاء» is the pronoun of the object, returning to the Prophet ﷺ. «المَأْوَى» is the fāʿil, in the sense: "the sheltering of Allah the Exalted covered him". It was also said: the meaning is: "the night's lodging and the night enveloped him". It was also said: "it covered him with its shade and he entered into it". ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, rejected this reading, and a group followed her, saying: «أجَنَّ اللَّهُ مَنْ قرأها» ("may Allah drive mad whoever reads it"). When a reading is established from the like of these, there is no way to reject it; but what is in use is «أَجَنَّه» in the quadriliteral; if it is used in the triliteral, it is made transitive with «على», as in His saying {فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ الليل} [الأنعام: 76]. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is irregular, and what is in use is «أجنَّه»." Discussion of this root was given earlier in al-Anʿām. «إذ يَغْشَى» is accusative by «رآه». His saying «ما يَغْشَى» is like His saying {مَآ أوحى} [النجم: 10].

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {الكبرى}: There are two views on it. The first, which is the apparent one: that «الكبرى» is the object of «رأى», and {مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِ} is a fronted ḥāl (circumstantial). The implied sense: "He saw the greatest signs from the signs of his Lord." The second: that {مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِ} is the object of the seeing and «الكُبْرى» is an adjective of the signs of his Lord. This plural may be qualified with the attribute of the single feminine, and what made it good here is that it is a verse-end. The like of it was mentioned earlier in Ṭā Hā [الآية: 23], as in {لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا الكبرى}.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {اللات}: the name of an idol. It was said that it belonged to Thaqīf in al-Ṭāʾif; Qatāda said this. It was said: in Nakhla. It was said: in ʿUkāẓ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya favoured the first by the saying of the poet:
4129 - وفَرَّتْ ثَقِيْفٌ إلى لاتِها ... بمُنْقَلَبِ الخائبِ الخاسرِ
(Thaqīf fled to its Lāt, with the return of the disappointed and the losing.)
The «ألف» and «لام» in «اللات» are redundant (zāʾida) and inseparable. As for his saying «إلى لاتِها», he dropped it because of the annexation. Are it and «العُزَّى» proper names by original imposition, or predominant attributes? There is disagreement, and on this depends whether «أل» may be dropped or not. If we say that they were not attributes originally, «أل» is not dropped from them; if we say that they are attributes, and that «أل» is for hinting at the attribute, it is allowed; and on either assumption «أل» is redundant. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said: they are two predominant attributes like «الحارث» and «العباس», so «أل» is not redundant." End.
This is an error, because the «أل» of hinting at the attribute is explicitly stated to be redundant, in the sense that it has no effect of definiteness.
There is disagreement about the «تاء» of «اللات». It was said: it is original, and its origin is from «لات يليتُ», so its «ألف» is from «ياء», for the root «ل ي ت» exists. It was said: it is added, and it is from «لَوَى يَلْوي», because they used to turn («يَلْوُوْن») their necks toward it, or bend («يَلْتَوون») over it, that is, devote themselves to it; and its origin is «لَوَيَة», its final radical having been dropped, so its «ألف» on this is from «واو». The readers differed over pausing on its «تاء»: al-Kisāʾī paused on it with «هاء» and the rest with «تاء», and this is built on the two earlier views: whoever held its «تاء» to be original kept it in pausing like the «تاء» of «بَيْت», and whoever held it to be added paused on it with «هاء». The majority read its «تاء» light. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, Abū al-Jawzāʾ, Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read the «تاء» with shadda. It was said: he was a man who used to mix («يَلُتُّ») barley meal and feed the pilgrims, so it is originally an active participle that came to predominate for this man; he used to sit by a rock, and when he died the rock was named after him and worshipped besides Allah the Exalted.
«العُزَّى» is on the pattern «فُعْلى» from «العِزّ» (might); it is the feminine of «الأَعَزّ», like «الفُضْلى» and «الأفضل», and it is the name of an idol. It was also said: a tree that was worshipped.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {وَمَنَاةَ}: Ibn Kathīr read «مَناءَة» with a hamza with fatḥa after the «ألف»; the rest read it with an «ألف» alone. It was a rock that was worshipped besides Allah. As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr, its derivation is from «النَّوْء», which is rain, because they would seek rain at it («الأَنْواء»); its pattern is then «مَفْعَلَة», so its «ألف» is from «واو», its hamza original and its «ميم» added. They quoted for this:
4130 - ألا هل أَتَى تَيْمَ بنَ عبدِ مَناءة ... علَى النَّأْيِ فيما بيننا ابنُ تميمِ
(Has the son of Tamīm reached Taym ibn ʿAbd Manāʾa, despite the distance between us?)
Abū ʿUbayd rejected the reading of Ibn Kathīr and said: "I have not heard the hamza." I say: others have heard it, and the verse is evidence against him.
As for the reading of the majority, its derivation is from «مَنى يَمْني», that is, he poured; because the blood of the sacrifices was poured at it. They quoted Jarīr:
4131 - أزيدَ مَناةَ تُوْعِدُ يا بنَ تَيْمٍ ... تَأَمَّلْ أين تاهَ بك الوعيدُ
(Do you threaten Zayd Manāt, O son of Taym? Consider where the threat has led you astray.)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its «ألف» is from «ياء», from your saying «مَنَى يَمْني» when one decreed, and it may be from «واو», from which comes «مَنَوان»." So its pattern on the short reading is «فَعْلة».
«والأُخْرى» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مَناة». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«والأُخْرى» is emphasis, because the third can only be 'another'." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«والأُخْرى» is a censure; it is the last, of low rank, as in His saying {قَالَتْ أُخْرَاهُمْ} [الأعراف: 38], that is, their lowly ones to their nobles; and it is possible that primacy and precedence, in their view, belonged to Lāt and ʿUzzā." End. There is room for objection in this, because «الأخرى» only indicates otherness and has no reference to praise or blame; if any of this appears, it is due to an external indication. It was also said: «الأُخْرى» is an adjective of «العُزَّى», because the second is "other" relative to the first. Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "There is fronting and delaying in it", that is, "ʿUzzā the other, and Manāt the third", but there is no need for that, because the default is non-occurrence.
«أرأيت» has the sense of «أَخْبِرْني» ("tell me"), so it takes two objects: the first, «اللات» and what is conjoined to it; the second, the interrogative clause in His saying «أَلكُمُ الذَّكَرَ». If it is said: no pronoun returns from this clause to the first object, the answer is that His saying «وله الأنثى» is equivalent to «وله هذه الأصنام», even if the original construction was «ألكم الذَّكَر وله هُنَّ», that is, those idols; this overt noun was preferred only because it falls at the head of a verse-ending.
Al-Zajjāj made the second object omitted, for he said: "The way of joining this verse to what precedes it is that He says: tell me about your gods, do they have anything of the power and greatness with which the Lord of Might was described in the earlier verses?" End. On this, His saying «ألكم الذَّكَرُ» is connected to what precedes it in meaning, not in grammar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made the seeing here seeing with the eye, saying: "It is from seeing with the eye, because he referred to visible bodies; had it been the «أَرَأَيْتَ» that is a request for an opinion, it would not have been transitive." This is a muddled statement, and the discussion of it was given in full earlier in al-Anʿām and elsewhere.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {ضيزى}: Ibn Kathīr read «ضِئْزَى» with a hamza with sukūn; the rest read it with a «ياء» in its place. Zayd ʿAlī [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably Zayd ibn ʿAlī] read «ضَيْزَى» with fatḥa on the «ضاد» and a «ياء» with sukūn. As for the reading of the majority, it may be from «ضازه يَضيزه» when he wronged him and acted unjustly toward him. So the meaning of «ضِيْزَى» is unjust. The poet said:
4132 - ضازَتْ بنو أُسْدٍ بحُكْمِهِمُ ... إذ يَجْعلون الرأسَ كالذَّنَبِ
(The Banū Asad acted unjustly in their judgement, when they made the head like the tail.)
On this, two views are possible. The first: that it is an attribute on the pattern «فُعْلى» with ḍamma on the first radical, and the first radical was given kasra so that the «ياء» would be sound, like «بِيض». If it is said: and why [Translator's note: the source reads «فإن قيل: وأيُّ فالجوابُ», which is incomplete; the objection is not preserved], the answer is that Sībawayh reported that no attribute on the pattern «فِعْلى» with kasra on the first radical has occurred, only with ḍamma, such as «حُبْلى», «أُنْثى», «رُبَّى» and the like. But others have reported that among attributes: Thaʿlab reported «مِشْية حِيْكى» and «رجلٌ كِيْصَى», and others reported «امرأةٌ عِزْهى» and «امرأة سِعْلى». This does not refute him, because Sībawayh says «حِيْكى» and «كِيْصى» are like what he says of «ضيزَى», so that the «ياء» may be sound; and as for «عِزْهَى» and «سِعْلى», the well-known forms of them are «سِعْلاة» and «عِزْهاة».
The second view: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like «ذِكْرى». Al-Kisāʾī said: one says «ضازَ يَضيز ضِيْزَى» like «ذَكَر يَذْكُر ذِكْرى». It may also be from «ضَأَزَه» with the hamza, as in the reading of Ibn Kathīr, but with its hamza lightened, even though changing a hamza like this into «ياء» is not among the principles of all the readers; it is a dialect that was adhered to, so they read with it. The meaning of «ضَأَزَه يَضْأَزُه» with the hamza is: he diminished him through injustice and wrong, which is close to the first. Among those who allowed that the «ياء» be a replacement for a hamza was Abū ʿUbayd, and that its origin be «ضُوْزَى» with «واو», because «ضازَه يَضُوْزُه ضُوْزى», «ضازه يَضِيْزُه ضِيْزى» and «ضَأَزه يَضْأَزُه ضَأْزاً» were heard; al-Kisāʾī reported all that, and Abū ʿUbayd reported «ضِزْتُه» and «ضُزْته» with kasra and with ḍamma on the first radical. The «ضاد» of «ضُوْزَى» was given kasra because ḍamma is heavy with «واو», and they did that to reach by it the changing of the «واو» into «ياء». Al-Akhfash quoted, on the dialect of the hamza:
4133 - فإن تَنْأَ عَنَّا نَنْتَقِصْك وإن تَغِبْ ... فَسَهْمُكَ مَضْؤُوْزٌ وأَنْفُكَ راغِمُ
(If you go far from us we will diminish you, and if you are absent, your share is cut short and your nose is in the dust.)
«ضِئْزَى» in the reading of Ibn Kathīr is a maṣdar used as an attribute, and it cannot be an original attribute, because of what was mentioned from Sībawayh. If it is said: why is it not said of «ضِئْزى», with kasra and hamza, that its origin is «ضُئْزَى» with ḍamma and the first radical was given kasra, as was said of it with the «ياء»? The answer: nothing here requires a change, since ḍamma with the hamza is not found as heavy as with a quiescent «ياء»; and «ضُوْزَى» with ḍamma on the «ضاد» with «واو» or with the hamza was heard from them.
As for the reading of Zayd, it may be a maṣdar used as an attribute like «دَعْوى», and it may be an attribute like «سَكْرى» and «عَطْشَى».

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {إِنْ هِيَ}: there are two views on «هي». The first: that it is a pronoun for the idols, that is, "they are nothing but names, with no real referents beneath them, because you claim divinity for what is the farthest of things from it and the most contrary to it", as in His saying {مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إِلاَّ أَسْمَآءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ} [يوسف: 40]. The second: that it is a pronoun for the names, which are Lāt, ʿUzzā and Manāt, and they mean by them the names of the gods; that is: "these names are nothing but names which you named according to your whims and desires, and you have no proof of the soundness of their naming to which you can hold"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«أسماء» must mean 'possessors of names', because of His saying «سَمَّيْتُموها», for a name is not itself named."
His saying: {إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ}: the majority read it in the third person, as an iltifāt (shift) from addressing them to speaking about them as absent, to belittle them. ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ṭalḥa, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Wathāb read it in the second person, which is good and agreeable.
His saying: {وَمَا تَهْوَى الأنفس}: a conjunction (nasaq) on «الظن», and «ما» is a maṣdar particle, or has the sense of «الذي».
His saying: {وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ الهدى}: It is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يَتَّبعون», that is, "they follow conjecture and the desire of the soul while the opposite of that is present, namely the coming of guidance from their Lord". It is also permissible that it be parenthetical, since His saying «أم للإِنسان» is connected to His saying {وَمَا تَهْوَى الأنفس}, and it is the disjunctive «أم», which is implied as «بل» and the hamza according to the correct view. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning of the hamza in it is denial, that is: man does not get whatever he wishes."
